tasks.short: Work out material, overhead and other costs from quotes and price lists.

today.trigger: A supplier sends a quotation or a new price list, or a site asks what a shipment, a storage week or a consumable will cost.
steps: Save the PDF or spreadsheet from Outlook into the cost folder on SharePoint.
Type the rates into the workbook: article, unit, site, and whether it is packaging, fuel, maintenance or agency labour.
Look up the overhead percentage the controller last used for that site.
Compare the new total with the last accepted price and, where there is one, with the customer contract rate.
Mail the figure to the buyer or the controller and file the sheet.
drudgery: Retyping rows from PDF price lists into Excel.
Hunting SharePoint for the overhead file that is still current.
Reconciling two or three copies of the same workbook.
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes into retyping and into finding the overhead rate that still applies. The arithmetic itself is short.

lenses.faster: Reading the quotation into lines and retyping it disappear. Applying the overhead key and comparing it with the last accepted price takes about half the time this task takes today, because every result is still checked before anyone uses it.
lenses.autonomous: A new quotation or price list in the AP mailbox starts it. The model fills the lines and a formula applies the site overhead and the last price. The bookkeeper approves each result before the rate is used on a supplier invoice or a customer charge.
lenses.ambitious: The accept-or-reject decision on a supplier price change, on the day the list arrives, for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Demand would grow in months when fuel and agency rates move, because purchasing would ask for a same-day answer if it stayed cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping price-list rows. The work they want more of is the rate jump that changes a customer contract or a CAO-linked agency rate.
lenses.options: Costing the same quotation with the site overhead, the customer-contract overhead and the activity overhead changes whether the job sits above the contract rate and whether purchasing accepts the supplier price.
lenses.altitude: The week has a short queue of price changes in place of a workbook rebuild. They may accept a rate inside the tolerance and must send anything outside it to the controller. The job is more expert on cost and contract rates, and less of it is spreadsheet assembly.
reach: The accountant's routine allocation of packaging and fuel to site cost centres, once the bookkeeper knows the allocation key the controller uses.
The FP&A analyst's price-effect line for warehouse consumables, once they know which forecast line each article hits.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper can tell a one-off spot buy from the new seasonal list, and can tell a CAO-linked agency rate at Tilburg from a Rotterdam fuel surcharge that should not be averaged across sites. A mis-read unit, a pallet price used as a piece price, has to be caught by the person before it reaches a customer invoice.
tasks.pattern_why: The quotation arrives as a PDF or a mail. One model call turns it into lines with a supplier, a unit and a price. The overhead and the total are then a formula. The path does not branch enough to need an agent.

in_practice.trigger: A quotation, an estimate or a price list arrives in the AP mailbox or is dropped in the SharePoint cost folder.
steps: The model reads the document into lines: supplier, article, unit, price, site and date.
A formula applies that site's overhead key and sets the line next to the last accepted price and any customer contract rate.
Lines inside tolerance queue for the bookkeeper. Lines outside tolerance go to the controller with the old rate and the new rate.
The bookkeeper accepts or corrects the lines.
Accepted rates update the AFAS price record that accounts payable and receivable use.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves every cost before it is used. A rate outside tolerance also needs the controller.
data_needed: The current overhead key per site and per activity.
The last accepted price and the date it started.
Customer contract rates where the cost will be recharged.
The tolerance the controller has agreed.
Which agency rates are tied to the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer scale.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS price history, plus a monthly rate-change log on SharePoint with the source file and the person who approved it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Scan & herken turns a supplier PDF that has no UBL into structured fields, finds the supplier from KvK, VAT number and IBAN, and leaves the gaps for a person.
Dutch invoice-automation results fall short of touchless processing where each administration has its own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions, and where PDFs keep arriving.
Once unit rates and an overhead key sit in a table, the cost total is ordinary arithmetic.

risks: A mis-read unit prices a whole customer contract wrong and still looks tidy in the total.
An out-of-date overhead key makes every quote wrong in the same direction, so a check against last month still passes.

A supplier PDF can carry a contact's personal data. The extract has to stay in the company tenant, with a person approving the rate, to meet AVG and the EU AI Act's expectation of human oversight on this limited-risk use.
research_questions: How many quotations and price lists arrive in a month, and what share is a PDF rather than a structured file?
Is the overhead key written down per site and activity, or does the controller choose it each time?
Which of these calculated costs flow into a customer invoice, and who is allowed to change that rate?
On a sample of 30 recent quotes, how many would a model have read with the right unit, site and price?

tasks.short: Reconcile the Rabobank statement to the open invoices.

today.trigger: Rabobank sends the CAMT.053 statement, usually each morning, and again in the days before the month locks.
steps: Import the statement into AFAS Profit.
Match lines that carry a payment reference or an obvious invoice number.
For the rest, search open items by IBAN, amount and date, including part-payments and batched receipts.
Split staffing-agency receipts and payments between the ordinary account and the g-rekening.
Code bank costs and anything still unknown, and leave the month-end list for the controller.
drudgery: Ticking lines that already match on amount and reference.
Searching the open-item list for a reference the customer shortened.
Rebuilding the same exception spreadsheet at month end.
today.time_sinks: The clean majority of lines takes little judgment and most of the clicking. The slow part is a short list of part-payments, unknown receipts and agency batches.

lenses.faster: Searching the open items for a reference, an IBAN or an exact amount disappears where AFAS can match them. The exception list, the g-rekening split and the month-end look take just over a third of the time this reconciliation takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The CAMT.053 import from Rabobank starts it. AFAS matches on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums, inside the tolerance, and posts those lines. Unmatched lines, amounts over tolerance, IBAN-name warnings and agency splits wait for the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A same-morning list of unmatched receipts, by customer and by site, for the credit and collections officer. Demand would grow, because in peak season that officer would chase a short-pay the same day and would ask for the list every morning if it stayed cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking lines that already match. The work they want more of is the odd receipt: the wrong site, the short-pay on damaged freight, the agency batch.
lenses.options: Showing the same leftover as a part-payment, a duplicate, or a payment on account changes whether collections calls the customer, accounts payable stops a run, or the cash stays on account.
lenses.altitude: The morning starts from the unmatched queue. They may post a match inside the tolerance the controller set, and they have to stop a line with an IBAN-name warning or a g-rekening shortfall. The job is more expert on those exceptions, and the ticking is gone from the week.
reach: The accountant's month-end tie of the bank control account to the general ledger, once the bookkeeper knows which reconciling items the auditor expects to see.
The credit and collections officer's coding of what an unmatched receipt relates to, once they know the dispute codes. The call to the customer remains that officer's.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper can tell a short-pay that is a damage claim from a short-pay that is a missing credit note, because they know the customer and the site. They have to refuse a payment after an IBAN-name warning when the master data is wrong, and they have to send the wage-tax and VAT part of an agency payment to the g-rekening. The match rules post the clean lines and leave these.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already matches bank lines with written rules: reference, IBAN, invoice number, then amount. A model does not match those better than the rules, and the residual is an exception queue.

in_practice.trigger: The daily CAMT.053 import from Rabobank lands in AFAS Profit.
steps: AFAS matches each line on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then on oldest-first sums, using exact amounts unless the agreed tolerance applies.
Matched lines clear the open item.
The bookkeeper receives the rest: part-payments, unknown receipts, amounts over tolerance, IBAN-name warnings, and agency payments.
The bookkeeper splits the agency payment so the wage-tax and VAT part is paid from or into the g-rekening, and codes what is truly unknown.
Cleared receipts update the open items the credit and collections officer sees the same morning.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper clears every unmatched line, every IBAN-name warning and every g-rekening split. The controller reviews the month-end reconciliation. Matches inside the rules post on their own.
data_needed: CAMT.053 statements.
Open payable and receivable items with payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount.
The tolerance the controller and the auditor have agreed.
Agency invoices with the wage-tax and VAT portion marked.
The supplier IBAN master and any recent IBAN change.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank-matching log: rule used, tolerance, person who cleared an exception, and the data they saw.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then oldest-first sums, for exact amounts unless a tolerance is set, and sends the misses to a person.

A hirer can be held liable for a staffing agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT, and limits that exposure with a payment-behaviour statement, proper records, and payment of that part into the agency's g-rekening.
Since October 2025, banks check the payee name against the IBAN. A payer who confirms the payment after a warning is not blocked by the bank.

risks: A wide tolerance clears the wrong invoice and hides a real open item.
Confirming an IBAN-name warning after a fraudster changes supplier master data still sends the money. The bank will not stop a confirmed payment.
Paying an agency without the g-rekening split leaves Noordhaven exposed if that agency does not pay its wage tax or VAT.
Applying a receipt to the wrong site hides a dispute and flatters days sales outstanding.
research_questions: What share of Rabobank lines does AFAS already match with no tolerance, and what are the top five reasons for a miss?
What tolerance will the controller and the auditor sign, in euros and as a percentage?
How many agency payments a month need a g-rekening split, and is that split written on the invoice?
How many IBAN-name warnings appear per month, and who is allowed to confirm one?

tasks.short: Build the cash, spend, creditor and debtor tables.

today.trigger: The controller, FP&A or a site manager asks for the weekly cash, spend, creditor or debtor figures, or for a cut of profit and loss.
steps: Export creditors, debtors, cash and the relevant ledger lines from AFAS.
Paste them into the workbook that finance used last time.
Rebuild the pivots by site, supplier, customer and period.
Check the totals against the AFAS control accounts and fix the rows that broke the pivot.
Send the workbook by mail or drop it in the close folder on SharePoint.
drudgery: Copying the same AFAS export into Excel every week.
Repairing pivot ranges and lookup errors after an account code changes.
Re-cutting the same aging because someone wanted one extra column.
today.time_sinks: The export and the workbook take the time. The check against AFAS is shorter, and it is the part that catches a wrong total.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the weekly cash book, the creditor and debtor aging and the spend table in Excel disappears. The tie-out to AFAS and the occasional one-off cut take about two fifths of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract starts it. Power BI refreshes the standard tables, and a check compares them with the AFAS control accounts. A table that ties is available to finance. A table that does not tie waits for the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly aging of small-supplier invoices against the statutory 30-day cap, for the controller. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because the controller would use it every month to see a breach before a supplier complains.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying exports and repairing pivots. The work they want more of is the table that explains a real swing in cash or in overdue freight invoices.
lenses.options: Cutting the same debtor balance by customer, by site and by overdue bucket changes whether the credit officer calls the customer or a site manager looks for a local dispute.
lenses.altitude: A standing pack replaces the weekly rebuild. They may mark the cash, creditor and debtor tables ready when the totals tie to AFAS, and they have to hold a pack that does not. The controller remains the person who releases a profit figure. The job is more expert on tie-outs and less occupied with workbook assembly.
reach: The FP&A analyst's monthly actuals extract for payables and receivables, once the bookkeeper knows which AFAS accounts map to which forecast lines.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper can see when a table ties and still misleads: a credit note in the wrong period, an agency invoice booked gross of the g-rekening, or a receipt still unmatched so a customer looks overdue. That reading has to stay with the person who lets the pack go out.
tasks.pattern_why: The columns, the sites and the filters are fixed, and AFAS already holds the rows. A saved extract and a tie-out check compile the table. A model is not required.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly refresh of the AFAS extract that already feeds Power BI.
steps: Power BI refreshes the cash, spend, creditor and debtor tables by site and by period.
A check compares those totals with the AFAS control accounts and with the prior day.
A pack that ties is marked ready for the controller and for FP&A.
A pack that does not tie is held, and the bookkeeper opens the difference.
A one-off audit cut that has no saved layout is still built by the bookkeeper.
The small-supplier aging flags invoices that would pass 30 days.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper holds any standard pack that fails the tie-out. The controller releases any table that states profit or loss. One-off audit samples are built and checked by the bookkeeper.
data_needed: The nightly AFAS extract of creditors, debtors, cash and ledger lines.
The control-account totals from AFAS for the same moment.
A marker for which suppliers are small firms under the 30-day rule.
Site and cost-centre codes for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Who is allowed to see customer-level detail.
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI refresh log and a short tie-out note in the SharePoint close folder: extract time, totals, and who held or released the pack.

evidence.claim: A repeating table of cash, payables and receivables can be produced from a fixed ledger extract and a fixed layout, without a model.
Processes that look automatic still mis-state the books when ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions differ by administration and PDFs keep arriving.
In a Wolters Kluwer survey of 594 respondents, 70% still approve invoices on paper or by email, and 43% say this regularly delays payment.
Under BW 6:119a a large company may not agree a payment term longer than 30 days with a small supplier.

risks: A pack can tie to the ledger and still be wrong if the underlying coding is wrong.
An aging that ignores the small-supplier flag will hide a breach of the 30-day rule.
Customer-level debtor lists can be personal data where the customer is a sole trader, so a wide SharePoint link would breach AVG.
If Noordhaven still approves invoices by email, the pack is only as current as that approval queue.
research_questions: Which of these tables already exist in Power BI, and which are still rebuilt in Excel each week?
Do the Power BI totals tie to the AFAS trial balance without a manual bridge?
Does Noordhaven still approve any invoices on paper or by email, and does that delay the tables?
Which customers on the debtor list are sole traders, and who is allowed to see that list?

tasks.short: Prepare the trial balance before the month locks.

today.trigger: Close starts, after accounts payable, accounts receivable, the bank and the payroll interface have been posted.
steps: Run the trial balance in AFAS and export it to the close workbook.
Tick creditor, debtor, bank, VAT, stock and suspense back to their sub-ledgers.
List anything that does not roll forward from last month.
Chase the site or the colleague who owns the late item, and book the correction.
Send the workbook to the controller before the period locks.
drudgery: Exporting the trial balance and ticking accounts that already match.
Re-running the same export after each late journal.
Chasing three sites for the same missing piece of paperwork.
today.time_sinks: The time sits in the accounts that do not tie, and in waiting for late invoices from the sites. Producing the trial balance itself is a short step in AFAS.

lenses.faster: Running the trial balance, exporting it and ticking the accounts that already match disappear. Opening the failed control accounts and writing the note to the controller take about thirty percent of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar starts it on the first working day. AFAS runs the trial balance and compares each control account with its sub-ledger. Accounts that tie are marked clear. Every account that fails waits for the bookkeeper, and the controller locks the period only after that list is accepted.
lenses.ambitious: A working-day-2 list, for the warehouse administrators at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, of accruals and receipts still open, including paperwork from the night shift. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because each site would use it every month to book before the lock.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking accounts that already agree. The work they want more of is the suspense or VAT difference that actually moves the month.
lenses.options: Classifying the same leftover as a timing difference, a missing accrual or a wrong VAT code changes whether the controller can lock the period or the month has to stay open.
lenses.altitude: Close week becomes a failed-account list across three sites. They may mark a control account clear when it ties under the controller's rule, and they have to hold the lock while one fails. The job is more expert on what a difference does to the result, and the re-foot is gone.
reach: The accountant's first pass over the payable, receivable, VAT and bank controls on the close checklist, once the bookkeeper can apply the controller's materiality.

tasks.human_edge: The same euro difference can be a timing item the close can absorb or an error that misstates the month. The bookkeeper, using the controller's materiality, is the person who can tell those apart. AFAS can only show that two numbers differ.
tasks.pattern_why: A trial balance and a sub-ledger tie-out are equalities. AFAS can run them on a schedule. A model adds nothing to a balance that has to foot.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar reaches the first working day of the new month.
steps: AFAS runs the trial balance and compares creditor, debtor, bank, VAT, stock and suspense with their sub-ledgers.
Accounts that tie are marked clear, with the sub-ledger total stored next to the general-ledger total.
Accounts that differ land on a list with the amount, the site and the journals posted since the prior lock.
The bookkeeper corrects or explains each failed account, and sends site-owned gaps to the warehouse administrators.
The controller locks the period when the list is empty or the remaining items are accepted as timing.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper clears or explains every failed control account. The controller locks the period. A forced clearing of suspense needs the controller as well.
data_needed: Posted journals for payables, receivables, bank, payroll interface, VAT and stock.
Sub-ledger totals at the same cut-off.
The materiality the controller allows for a timing item.
Which site owns each open accrual or missing receipt.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS close checklist: account, difference, explanation, who cleared it, and the data they used.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 posts and approves for payment a one-to-one match with an order or a receipt, which is what lets the creditor control account tie to the sub-ledger. The published description gives no match rate.
Touchless posting disappoints where ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions differ by administration, so a balanced report can still hide open items.
Routine payable processing can run with people on the exceptions, provided every decision is logged with the data that was used.

risks: A check pointed at the wrong sub-ledger gives a false pass and the period locks on a broken control.
Late invoices from a night shift, booked after the check, reopen the difference.
Someone clears suspense to empty the list. The log and a second person on forced clearings are what stop that.
The payroll interface can post after the trial balance has already been marked clear.
research_questions: How many control accounts fail in a normal month, and how long do those failures take to clear?
What materiality does the controller use before a difference may stay as a timing item?
Does the AFAS trial balance already tie to Power BI, or is there a second close file in Excel?
Are the VAT reverse-charge account and the g-rekening among the accounts that fail most often?

tasks.short: Pull actuals and the last budget together for FP&A.

today.trigger: FP&A opens a budget round or asks for a fresh actuals pack after the month locks.
steps: Export actuals from AFAS by ledger, site and month.
Find the previous budget workbook on SharePoint and paste actuals onto its lines.
Add known changes from new price lists, the CAO and the agency invoices.
Flag lines that do not map, and ask FP&A or the controller what they are.
Hand the workbook to the FP&A analyst.
drudgery: Finding the budget version FP&A actually uses.
Pasting actuals line by line onto last year's layout.
Splitting a lump agency invoice across three sites by hand.
today.time_sinks: The paste and the mapping take the hours. The argument about whether a line is comparable takes the judgment, and it is a smaller share of the clock.

lenses.faster: The download from AFAS and the line-by-line paste into the budget workbook disappear. Checking accounts that moved, and attaching known price and CAO changes, still takes about half the time.
lenses.autonomous: The budget-cycle date on the finance calendar starts the extract. A fixed query lays actuals, the previous budget and open purchase commitments next to each other by site and ledger. The bookkeeper approves the pack before FP&A loads it.
lenses.ambitious: A cost pack by staffing agency and by site, for the FP&A analysts, covering the swing from 150 to 300 flex workers. Demand would grow in peak season if it were cheap, because FP&A would then want it every month and not once a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting last year's workbook. The work they want more of is the conversation about why fuel, overtime or agency cost actually moved.
lenses.options: Showing the same agency spend at last year's rate, at the new price list and at peak-season volume changes whether FP&A holds the warehouse budget or asks the business for more.
lenses.altitude: They maintain the mapping from AFAS accounts to budget lines and stop pasting the workbook. They may flag a line as not comparable before FP&A treats the gap as a variance. FP&A still owns the forecast number. The job is more expert on the chart of accounts.
reach: The FP&A analyst's first-cut actuals-versus-budget for fuel, packaging and agency labour, once the bookkeeper knows how the forecast phases the season.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper knows which actual must not be copied forward: a one-off claim, a hall closed at one site, a CAO wage increase, or an agency invoice that covers two months. A roll-forward will treat each of those as the new run-rate. Marking them has to stay with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is a join of ledger actuals, the previous budget and known price files. Those joins can be written down. A model is not what makes the columns add up.

in_practice.trigger: The finance calendar reaches a budget round, or FP&A asks for the actuals pack after lock.
steps: AFAS extracts actuals, the previous budget and open commitments by ledger, month and site.
The mapping marks accounts that are new, closed or moved since the last pack.
Known price-list changes and the CAO rate change are attached as separate columns, not buried in the actual.
Agency cost is split by agency and site, with the g-rekening portion in its own column, using the portal hours where they tie to the invoice.
The bookkeeper reviews every unmapped or not-comparable line and approves the pack.
FP&A loads only the approved version.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves each pack before FP&A uses it. FP&A decides the forecast. A line the bookkeeper has marked not comparable is not a variance until FP&A accepts that mark.
data_needed: Actuals by ledger, month and site.
The previous budget version FP&A still treats as current.
The account-to-budget-line mapping.
Price-list and CAO changes already approved.
Agency invoices and portal hours for the three agencies, including the g-rekening share.
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint budget folder: version, extract time, mapping version, lines marked not comparable, and the bookkeeper's approval.

evidence.claim: Aligning actuals to a previous budget is a mapping from the ledger once the chart of accounts is stable. The judgment is which lines are not comparable.
A hirer limits liability for an agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT by keeping records and by paying that part into the g-rekening, so agency cost is not one number.
Automation of the underlying coding still fails where each administration uses its own ledger accounts and exceptions, which is also where a budget mapping breaks.

risks: A silent mapping change invents a variance, and FP&A builds the forecast on it.
Agency cost booked in the wrong month makes a seasonal peak look like a permanent run-rate.
Two versions of the workbook in SharePoint, with FP&A loading the wrong one.
Portal hours that do not tie to the AFAS invoice produce a site split nobody can defend.
research_questions: How much of this pack does the bookkeeper compile today, and how much does FP&A rebuild from scratch?
Has the chart of accounts stayed stable enough over the last year for a mapping to survive?
Can hours from the three agency portals be tied to AFAS invoices per site, or only as a company total?
Would FP&A load a pack the bookkeeper has approved without re-keying it?

tasks.short: Keep the stock ledger in line with receipts and counts.

today.trigger: A goods receipt is booked, a supplier invoice arrives, or a site sends its count of own materials such as packaging, fuel or spares.
steps: Match the goods receipt to the supplier invoice in AFAS.
Book issues of packaging and fuel to the site cost centre.
Compare the AFAS quantity with the count sheet from the site.
Book a small difference, or send a larger one to the controller with a proposed write-off.
Check that the stock value on the trial balance matches the stock ledger.
drudgery: Chasing a site for a receipt note that is already on the invoice.
Re-keying a count that arrived as a photo or a loose spreadsheet.
Holding the difference until quarter-end because close week is already full.
today.time_sinks: Matched receipts are repetitive. Most of the judgment, and much of the waiting, sits in count differences and in paperwork from the night shift.

lenses.faster: Matching a goods receipt to the supplier invoice and posting the standard issue disappear. The count difference and the write-off note stay, and they are about two thirds of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: A posted goods receipt or a returned count starts it. AFAS updates the stock ledger when the receipt and the invoice match inside tolerance. A count difference waits for the bookkeeper, and a write-off above the threshold also waits for the controller.
lenses.ambitious: The recount-or-write-off decision within a week of the count, at each site, while the shift still remembers the load. Demand would grow from a quarterly tidy-up to a monthly one if the pack were cheap. It would not become a daily decision. Own stock is small.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing receipt notes that are already on the invoice. The work they want more of is the difference that is a real loss: damage, a mis-pick, or stock that never arrived.
lenses.options: Treating the same shortage as a receipt not yet booked, as damage, or as a count error changes whether the site recounts or the month takes the cost.
lenses.altitude: The week barely changes, because this is a small task. At close they review a difference list in place of keying receipts. They may clear a difference inside the threshold and must send the rest to the controller. The job is more expert on cut-off and shrink, on a short list.
reach: The accountant's goods-received-not-invoiced accrual, once the bookkeeper knows the cut-off rule the controller uses.

tasks.human_edge: A shortage can be a receipt nobody booked, damage on the night shift, or a loss. The bookkeeper knows the site's paperwork and has to send a missing receipt back to be booked before anyone writes off stock. Above the threshold the controller has to agree, so one person cannot both hide a loss and clear it.
tasks.pattern_why: A receipt, an issue and a match to the invoice are transactions with a threshold. AFAS can post the ones that agree. Judgment starts when the count disagrees.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS posts a goods receipt, or a site returns its count of own materials.
steps: Where the receipt and the supplier invoice match inside tolerance, AFAS updates the stock quantity and the stock value.
Standard issues of packaging and fuel post to the site cost centre from the issue record.
A count that differs from AFAS opens a difference line with the site, the article and the quantity.
The bookkeeper sends a likely missing receipt back to the site, or proposes a write-off.
Write-offs above the threshold go to the controller with the count and the invoice.
The stock ledger total is one of the control accounts on the trial balance.
in_practice.human_gate: Matched receipts post on their own. The bookkeeper reviews every count difference. The controller approves a write-off above the threshold. The warehouse counts. The bookkeeper does not count their own write-off.
data_needed: Goods receipts and supplier invoices by site.
Count sheets for own materials: packaging, fuel, spares.
The write-off threshold in euros.
Whether the goods are Noordhaven stock or a customer's goods stored on site.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS stock journal, and the controller's approval on the write-off, with the count sheet stored in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS posts a one-to-one match with an order or a receipt and can approve it for payment. That is the goods-received side of the supplier invoice. No match rate is published.
Exception decisions in payables should stay with a person and be logged with the data used. A stock write-off is that kind of decision.
At about 22 hours a year per person, this task is a small financial stock record beside accounts payable. It is not the warehouse's day-to-day goods movement.

risks: Writing off a shortage that is really an unbooked receipt understates both stock and creditors.
Customer-owned goods on the warehouse floor get mixed into Noordhaven's stock value.
A night-shift count that never reaches AFAS leaves the ledger wrong until an audit count.
The same person must not count the stock and approve the write-off.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven carry own stock in AFAS, such as packaging, fuel and spares, or only a goods-received-not-invoiced balance?
Are customer goods stored at the three sites on Noordhaven's balance sheet?
What share of goods receipts already match an invoice with no person involved?
What write-off threshold will the controller let the bookkeeper clear alone?

tasks.short: Prepare the VAT figures and the other finance filings.

today.trigger: A VAT period ends, the accountant asks for the schedules, or a pension, employee-insurance or agency document is due.
steps: Pull revenue, input VAT, output VAT and reverse-charge balances from AFAS into a workbook.
Tick the totals to the VAT control account and list the invoices the check rejects.
Gather the g-rekening payments and the agency invoices that support the hirer's liability file.
For pension and employee-insurance amounts, ask the payroll specialist for the wage base and compare it with the supplier invoice.
Hand the schedules to the controller or the external accountant, who submits the return.
drudgery: Retyping ledger totals into the VAT working papers.
Chasing invoice copies that support a reverse-charge line.
Rebuilding the agency payment list from bank lines and portal PDFs.
today.time_sinks: Building the schedules takes about half the time. The rest is the odd invoice: foreign transport, a mixed-use cost, or an agency payment that does not match the g-rekening.

lenses.faster: Building the VAT schedules and the g-rekening listing from the ledger by hand disappears. Checking the exceptions and preparing the pack for signature take a bit over half the time, because a filing is not sent unread.
lenses.autonomous: The VAT-period date on the finance calendar starts the draft. AFAS fills the boxes from the tax codes and runs the control-account checks. Nothing is submitted until the controller, or the accountant they name, has approved that return.
lenses.ambitious: A quarterly inlenersaansprakelijkheid file per staffing agency, for the finance director: payment-behaviour statement on file, g-rekening share paid, invoices matched to hours. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because the exposure moves with every payment and with the swing from 150 to 300 flex workers.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping box totals. The work they want more of is the odd VAT code: reverse charge on foreign transport, a non-deductible cost, a private-use correction.
lenses.options: Treating one cross-border transport invoice as reverse-charged, as Dutch-standard-rated or as outside the scope changes the VAT due and whether it appears on the intra-EU listing.
lenses.altitude: A few times a year they review a drafted return and a short exception list. They may send a return back when a check fails. They do not gain the right to file it. The controller keeps the signature. The job is more expert on VAT exceptions and no more senior on the act of filing.
reach: The accountant's draft of the opgaaf intracommunautaire prestaties, once the bookkeeper knows which transport and warehousing services are intra-EU supplies or reverse-charged services.
The payroll specialist's tie-out of the industry pension invoice to the wage base, once the bookkeeper knows the CAO pension basis. The wage-tax return stays with payroll.

tasks.human_edge: A tax code on an invoice is not a filing position. Reverse charge on foreign transport, VAT that is not deductible, and whether the wage-tax and VAT part of an agency invoice was actually paid into the g-rekening are decisions for the bookkeeper and the controller. BSN and wage data have to stay inside AFAS with payroll and off any model.
tasks.pattern_why: The return is boxes filled from tax codes and control accounts. Those checks can be written down. A model must not invent a filing position, and pension forms carry a BSN, so they stay out of any model.

in_practice.trigger: The VAT-period date arrives, or the finance director asks for the quarterly agency-liability file.
steps: AFAS drafts the VAT boxes from the tax codes and compares them with the VAT control account, revenue and deductible cost.
Invoices that fail the check, including reverse charge and non-deductible VAT, go to the bookkeeper with the invoice and the code.
The g-rekening payments are listed per agency against the wage-tax and VAT portion on the invoices, with the payment-behaviour statement date.
Pension and employee-insurance invoices are matched to the totals the payroll specialist certifies. They are not re-keyed into a second form.
The bookkeeper signs the exception list. The controller, or the named accountant, submits the VAT return and keeps the filing receipt.
in_practice.human_gate: No government form is submitted by the software or by the bookkeeper alone. The controller or the named accountant approves each VAT return. Payroll submits wage-tax, pension and employee-insurance forms. The bookkeeper approves the schedules those filings use.
data_needed: VAT codes and the VAT control account.
Purchase and sales invoices with supplier VAT numbers, including cross-border transport.
G-rekening payments and the three agencies' invoices, split between labour and the wage-tax and VAT portion.
The payroll specialist's certified wage base for pension and employee insurance.
The payment-behaviour statement for each agency and its expiry date.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS VAT dossier and the Belastingdienst filing receipt in the SharePoint tax folder. The agency file sits beside it. No copy of a BSN goes into mail or into a model.

evidence.claim: A hirer can be liable for a staffing agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT. The Belastingdienst describes three limits: a payment-behaviour statement, the hirer's record-keeping duty, and payment of that part into the g-rekening.
The Dutch cabinet has chosen B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031. A PDF is not an e-invoice. This is not law yet.
A Peppol practitioner's reading of the proposals says buyers would report intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases within five days of receipt, and that a two-week approval round would miss that window.
Dutch wage-tax, pension and employee-insurance forms contain the BSN and belong in the payroll administration. They are a poor fit for a document model.

risks: A drafted VAT return filed without the controller understates or overstates VAT due, especially on reverse-charged transport.
An incomplete g-rekening file leaves Noordhaven holding the agency's wage tax and VAT if an agency fails.
Copying a pension form into mail or an external model leaks a BSN and breaches AVG.
E-invoicing reporting, if it becomes law on the announced dates, will need invoice data this process does not yet store. A slow approval round would miss a short reporting window.
research_questions: Who submits the VAT return today: the bookkeeper, the accountant, the controller, or an external advisor?
Which government forms does this role actually complete, and which sit with the payroll specialist?
Do any forms this role touches contain a BSN or wage data that must not leave AFAS?
Are the VAT codes on cross-border transport invoices consistent enough for a check to pass with only an exception review?

role.altitude: The three bookkeepers become the people who keep the payable and receivable sub-ledgers fit for a close the business trusts. Their week is exception queues: price changes, unmatched bank lines, failed control accounts, stock differences and VAT codes that are not plain. They may clear a case inside a threshold the controller has set. The controller still moves a threshold, releases a profit figure, signs a return and locks the period. The job is more expert on master data, cut-off and exceptions, and it keys far less.
reach: The accountant's goods-received-not-invoiced accrual and the first pass of the payable, receivable, bank and VAT controls, once they can apply the controller's materiality.
The credit and collections officer's identification of what an unmatched receipt relates to, once they know the dispute codes.
The FP&A analyst's actuals extract for fuel, packaging and agency cost by site, once they know how the forecast phases a season of 150 to 300 flex workers.
The payroll specialist's check that a pension-fund or agency invoice matches the certified wage base and the CAO rate.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about 13.5% of the role, roughly 216 hours a year per person. The rest of the job, invoice capture, payment runs and customer billing, still sets the week. Three people cannot also be FP&A, credit control and payroll. Separation of duties caps it: the same person cannot change a supplier IBAN, approve the payment and clear the bank line, or count stock and approve the write-off. Close still waits on other teams' accruals and on the sites sending documents late. A personal productivity score of the three bookkeepers would be a works-council matter, so the logs cover transactions and not a scoreboard.
skills_to_grow: AFAS match rules, invoice tolerances and the supplier master: KvK, VAT number and IBAN.
Dutch VAT on domestic and cross-border transport and warehousing, including reverse charge and the intra-EU listing.
The g-rekening split and the records that limit inlenersaansprakelijkheid for the three agencies.
The controller's materiality and close checklist, so a difference is either cleared or explained.
How FP&A maps the ledger to forecast lines, including the seasonal flex range.
The CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer rate structure, far enough to check an agency invoice and a pension-base tie-out.
role.ambitious_version: In a normal month the three bookkeepers work exception queues for three sites. Invoices and bank lines that match post under rules the controller has agreed. Each morning the credit officer sees unmatched cash. Tilburg and Venlo get the same creditor, debtor and consumable-cost pack as Rotterdam, and a working-day-2 list of what is still open. Each quarter the finance director has a file per agency showing the wage tax and VAT went to the g-rekening. Days to close then depend on real exceptions and on other teams' accruals. The forecast starts from actuals the sites recognise. The desk is more expert on those exceptions and smaller as a keying operation.
